title: Ravin bar Chinena (or Chanina)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: Hyman distinguishes two. One was Rav Chisda’s student, as in Ketubot 53a: Ravin bar Chanina sat before Rav Chisda and was saying in Rabbi Elazar’s name; he said to him: “If you had not told me in the name of a great man,” etc. In Menachot 30b: “Ravin bar Chinena (in Chullin 75b, bar Chanina) said that Ulla said that Rabbi Chanina said.” We find him in the Land of Israel, as in Chullin 122a: Rabbi Zeira was sitting and asking … Ravin bar Chinena said to him: “Thus said Ulla in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi…” Rabbi Zeira said to him: “You said one thing … come and see the difference between the forceful ones of the Land of Israel and the pious ones of Babylonia.” Hyman places the incident in the Land of Israel, where they called Rabbi Zeira “the pious one of Babylonia,” as Rashi explains; also, when Rabbi Zeira was in Babylonia he had not reached such a level and was only one of Rav Yehudah’s students.

There is also Ravin bar Chinena, the brother of Rav Dimi, Rava’s student, as in Bava Batra 13b: Rabbah (Ravin, Dikdukei Soferim) bar Chinena and Rav Dimi bar Chinena — their father left them two maidservants; they came before Rava. Hyman identifies this Ravin as the one mentioned in Pesachim 109b: “Rav Ashi said: Ravin bar Chinena told me: The table of the Temple was made of segments.”

notes.text: The two Ravins, date/land inference and assessment of Zeira are Hyman’s distinctions. The compressed Chullin exchange is retained without inventing omitted dialogue; Rabbah versus Dikdukei Soferim Ravin remains explicit.

Chullin 122a directly gives Ravin’s reply to Zeira in Ulla’s name and the forceful-Land-of-Israel versus pious-Babylonia contrast. It does not by itself establish two Ravins or Hyman’s dating and location assessment. The precise Rashi and Dikdukei Soferim readings and the Rabbah/Ravin emendation remain his reported evidence; omitted dialogue is not supplied.
